| **2.1.4** | Verify that any printable Unicode character, including language neutral characters such as spaces and Emojis are permitted in passwords. | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 521 | 5.1.1.2 |

Your application is not less secure without this, I recommend deleting.

@jmanico @elarlang @danielcuthbert @cronchie @ImanSharaf @ryarmst @TobiasAhnoff

comments.body:
There are 95 printable ASCII characters. There are over 65,536 or so printable unicode characters. Unicode allows for much stronger passwords. But I agree it's not absolutely necessary for secure software. I personally think we should leave this in.

But I can be convinced that in a world of MFA it doesn't matter as much.

It is considered "SHOULD" in NIST's latest draft so I would prefer to remove:
https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html#passwordver
I'd support deleting this as yeah, impact is minimal
